semantic_correction.stem: An average-risk client asks whether a formal monthly breast self-exam can replace recommended screening mammography. Which response best reflects current American Cancer Society guidance?

options.A: Yes. A formal monthly self-exam is an equivalent screening substitute when the client is comfortable examining the breasts.
options.B: No. Follow recommended mammography screening, remain familiar with usual breast appearance and feel, and report new changes promptly.
options.C: Yes. Either breast self-exam or clinical breast exam can replace mammography for an average-risk client who has no symptoms.
options.D: No. Avoid noticing breast changes between mammograms because self-awareness increases false-positive screening results.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Cancer Society breast-screening page was revised July 23, 2026. ACS states that breast self-exams and clinical breast exams are not sufficient for cancer screening and are unlikely to find breast cancer early in people at average risk. Mammography remains the recommended screening test for average-risk women according to the age-based ACS schedule. ACS also advises people to be familiar with how their breasts normally look and feel and to report changes to a health care provider right away. Therefore a formal self-exam does not replace recommended mammography, while breast awareness remains appropriate.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Distinguish breast awareness from formal breast self-examination and explain that self-exam does not replace recommended mammography screening for average-risk clients.

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Current ACS guidance does not treat formal breast self-examination or clinical breast examination as substitutes for recommended mammography in average-risk people, while encouraging breast awareness and prompt reporting of changes.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests the distinction between screening mammography and breast awareness without treating formal BSE/CBE as an equivalent screening modality.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. ACS states that breast self-exam is not sufficient as a screening substitute for average-risk people.
option_audit.B: Correct. It combines recommended mammography with ACS-supported breast awareness and prompt reporting of changes.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Neither formal BSE nor CBE replaces mammography for routine average-risk screening.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. ACS encourages familiarity with normal breast appearance/feel and prompt reporting of changes.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. B alone reflects both the current screening recommendation and the breast-awareness guidance.
cueing_check: All four choices are breast-screening counseling statements of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies B.
